belief: God’s blessing always shows up as health and wealth.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that God’s blessing always shows up as health and wealth, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Prosperity preaching that equates faith with financial success and good health. Social media that shows Christians’ blessings mainly as money, homes, and comfort. Feeling cursed or forgotten during illness or poverty. A culture that measures worth by success. Comparing your life with seemingly “blessed” people.
teaches: God does give good gifts, including health and provision, and we can thank Him for them. But Scripture describes blessing much more broadly. Jesus called the poor in spirit and those who mourn blessed. God has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing. Paul learned contentment in plenty and in want. Habakkuk chose to rejoice in God even when the crops failed. The greatest blessing is God Himself.
self_statements: If I were blessed, I’d be healthy and comfortable.
Poor or sick Christians must be doing something wrong.
God is blessing others, but not me.
Money shows how much God loves me.
My struggles mean I’m out of God’s favor.
errors: Limiting God’s blessing to money and health.
Measuring your blessing by other people’s possessions.
Assuming suffering means you are out of God’s favor.
Overlooking spiritual blessings you already have in Christ.
questions: Who did Jesus call blessed in Matthew 5?
What spiritual blessings do I have in Christ?
Was Paul unblessed when he was hungry and in need?
Could Habakkuk rejoice in God with empty fields?
Am I measuring blessing the way the world does?
What blessings do I have that money cannot buy?
Is God Himself enough for me?
truth: God’s blessing does not always show up as health and wealth. He has blessed me in Christ with every spiritual blessing. I can thank Him for physical provision and also rejoice in Him when I lack it. My greatest blessing is knowing God, and I can learn contentment in every situation.
hw_questions: What spiritual blessings do I have in Christ?
Could Habakkuk rejoice with empty fields?
Am I measuring blessing like the world does?
Is God Himself enough for me?
hw_truths: God has blessed me with every spiritual blessing in Christ.
My greatest blessing is God Himself.
I can rejoice in God in plenty or in want.
Blessing is more than health and wealth.
I can learn contentment in every situation.
I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
log: Each day, write three blessings that money cannot buy.
name_example: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed Sarah in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.
actions: and list every spiritual blessing Paul names.
Write your own “though” prayer like Habakkuk’s:
“Though ___, yet I will rejoice in the LORD.”
Spend time with someone who has little money but deep faith,
and notice what blessings they have.
Limit social media for one week
and notice whether you feel more or less blessed.
prayer: Father, thank You for every good gift, and most of all for Yourself. Help me reject the lie that Your blessing always shows up as health and wealth. Thank You for every spiritual blessing in Christ. Teach me contentment and joy in You, in plenty and in want. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
